epic.title: EPIC-32 Persist AI summaries in backend when computed (move from frontend-held cache to server-side store)
epic.functionalNeed: The AI-narrated summaries shown in the analysis (bullet-style perception panels on overview and category views) are produced on demand but kept only in the viewer's browser. The same summary is regenerated for every new viewer, every page reload, and every shared-link visitor. This EPIC keeps generation lazy but persists each summary on the server the moment it is computed, keyed by the exact combination of inputs that produced it.
scope: AI perception summaries on the overview and category views (the bullet-list panels)
Any other narrative block currently generated on demand and held only in the browser
Server-side persistence keyed by: analysisId + scope + categoryId (when scope=category) + country + set of selected AI engines
Invalidation of stored summaries when an analysis is rerun
Graceful handling of unreadable/corrupt stored summaries (regenerate + replace)
Email and export reuse of stored summaries
outOfScope: Precomputing summaries before a viewer requests them — generation stays lazy
Rule-based banners and insights that do not call an AI engine
Per-question detail panels, which read raw responses rather than summaries
stillOpen: Confirm the full inventory of narrative blocks beyond the perception panels that should move to the server-side store

stories.title: Generate and store on first request

userStory.as: a viewer opening a fresh analysis
userStory.want: the AI summary to be generated and saved server-side the first time it is requested
userStory.so: no one ever has to generate that same summary again

acceptanceCriteria.title: Summary generated and stored on first request
acceptanceCriteria.given: an AI summary has never been generated for a given filter combination
acceptanceCriteria.when: the first viewer opens that view
acceptanceCriteria.then: the summary is generated on demand and the result is stored on the server

acceptanceCriteria.title: Persist before returning
acceptanceCriteria.given: a summary is being generated for the first time
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result is persisted before being returned, not only returned to the requesting browser

technicalNotes: Generation stays lazy — no precomputation before a viewer requests the view
Cache key: { analysisId, scope: 'global'|'category', categoryId?, country, engineIds: string[] (sorted) }
Persistence step must complete (or be initiated durably) before response is sent

stories.title: Serve the stored summary on every repeat request

userStory.want: a previously generated summary to load instantly
userStory.so: I never wait for or pay for a regeneration of something already produced

acceptanceCriteria.title: Stored summary served on repeat request
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same filter combination has been generated before
acceptanceCriteria.when: any viewer opens that view from any browser, session, or shared link
acceptanceCriteria.then: the summary loads from the server with no new generation

acceptanceCriteria.title: Result identical to first requester
acceptanceCriteria.then: the result is identical to what the first requester received for the same inputs

technicalNotes: Applies to all request origins: any browser, any authenticated session, shared links
A stored summary is invalidated when the parent analysis is rerun

stories.title: Identify summaries by their full input combination

userStory.want: each distinct combination of inputs to have its own stored summary
userStory.so: switching country, category, or engine selection returns the summary that matches what I am looking at

acceptanceCriteria.title: Cache key covers all input dimensions
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is identified by the analysis, the scope (global or category), the category when the scope is a category, the country (or 'all'), and the set of selected AI engines

acceptanceCriteria.title: Previously seen combination served from store
acceptanceCriteria.given: a viewer switches to a country or category combination seen before
acceptanceCriteria.then: the matching stored summary loads instantly with no new generation

acceptanceCriteria.title: New engine subset triggers generation and storage
acceptanceCriteria.given: a viewer selects an engine subset that has not been seen before
acceptanceCriteria.then: the summary is generated and stored, and subsequent requests for that exact subset are served from the store

technicalNotes: Engine IDs set must be normalised (sorted, deduplicated) before hashing/storing
Switching a single dimension must produce a separate cache entry, not overwrite the previous one

stories.title: Treat an unreadable stored summary as a miss

userStory.want: a corrupt stored summary to be regenerated rather than shown
userStory.so: I never see broken or partial text

acceptanceCriteria.title: Corrupt entry treated as cache miss
acceptanceCriteria.given: a stored summary is corrupt or cannot be read back cleanly
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is treated as if no summary were stored and the summary is regenerated

acceptanceCriteria.title: Corrupt entry replaced after regeneration
acceptanceCriteria.given: an unreadable stored summary is regenerated
acceptanceCriteria.then: the corrupt entry is replaced with the fresh result

technicalNotes: Unreadable includes: JSON parse failure, missing required fields, encoding errors, truncated content
Replace operation must be atomic or ensure concurrent requests don't read the corrupt entry
No user-visible error — fallback is transparent

stories.title: Email and export reuse stored summaries

userStory.as: a recipient of the analysis-ready email or a generated export
userStory.want: the summary it contains to come from the same server-side store
userStory.so: the same text is consistent everywhere and is not generated again just for me

acceptanceCriteria.title: Email uses stored summary
acceptanceCriteria.then: it uses the stored summary, or generates and stores one if missing, and never bypasses the store

acceptanceCriteria.title: Export uses stored summary
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reads the stored summary rather than generating a new one on the fly

technicalNotes: Email and export pipelines must route through the same server-side store read path as the UI
If no stored summary exists at email/export time, apply the store-first pattern from US1.1
Text in email/export must be identical to what the UI shows for the same input combination
